analysis.session_summary: The window was dominated by yen strength and a firm dollar, with JPY +0.398% and USD +0.133%, while commodity FX lagged sharply (AUD -0.315%, NZD -0.190%). A Canada CPI miss at 0.2% vs 0.3% forecast weakened CAD 0.090% and pushed USD/CAD up 15 pips; Fed Chairman Warsh’s speech later knocked the USD 0.068% lower without a scoreable surprise. EUR/USD chopped through seven uncaused legs to close -23.3 pips near its low, reflecting no euro-specific driver. VIX rose 8.784% to 21.364, keeping risk-sensitive currencies on the defensive.

themes.evidence: JPY +0.398%, USD/JPY -42.4 pips; 'Suspected Yen Intervention' was top high-impact headline.
CPI actual 0.2% vs 0.3% forecast; CAD -0.093%; USD/CAD +15.0 pips at 7.44 sigma.

currency_drivers.USD: USD firmed 0.133% as DXY gained; Warsh speech only briefly softened it by 0.068%.
currency_drivers.EUR: EUR slipped 0.079% with no euro-specific catalyst; it held its range.
currency_drivers.JPY: JPY led with a 0.398% gain on suspected intervention and risk flows.
currency_drivers.GBP: GBP was flat at +0.008% with no clear catalyst, holding its range.
currency_drivers.AUD: AUD fell 0.315%, weakest among majors, with no domestic release to explain it.
currency_drivers.CAD: CAD weakened 0.093% after CPI missed at 0.2% vs 0.3% forecast.
currency_drivers.CHF: CHF rose 0.138% as a haven without domestic news; Warsh speech moved it.
currency_drivers.NZD: NZD fell 0.190% with no catalyst of its own; antipodean softness persisted.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD printed seven ragged legs in both directions but closed -23.3 pips near its low with no leg attributable to a clear catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: The normal CAD-negative reaction to a miss implies the market was positioned for a firmer CPI and a more hawkish BoC.
The measured 0.068% USD decline without a forecast suggests the speech was interpreted as slightly dovish, but the reaction lacked a scoreable surprise.

scenarios.name: USD holds bid as risk-off persists
scenarios.thesis: US data next reinforces the firm-dollar, risk-off tone; yen strength pauses and commodity FX stay heavy.
triggers: US Retail Sales m/m prints above 0.1%
Suspected yen intervention is not confirmed

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD already closed at 1.10045 near its low, and USD strength argues for another leg lower.
JPY's 0.398% surge may retrace if intervention headlines fade and USD demand resumes.
AUD is weakest, down 0.315%, and risk-off keeps it under pressure.

scenarios.name: Rangebound consolidation
scenarios.thesis: Markets wait for US retail and RBA, with no fresh catalyst to extend dollar or yen moves.
triggers: US Retail Sales in line at 0.1%

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD range was 36.2 pips; no catalyst should keep it inside.
USD/JPY range 57.6 pips; yen intervention ambiguity caps both directions.
USD/CAD range 55.9 pips; after CPI, CAD lacks fresh driver.

scenarios.name: Risk recovery and USD pullback
scenarios.thesis: VIX fades, the Warsh speech's dovish read catches up, and beaten-down AUD/NZD bounce.
triggers: RBA Bullock pushes back on cuts

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD can recover the day's 23.3 pip decline if USD softens.
AUD/USD fell 30.3 pips; a risk recovery would retrace that.
USD/JPY fell 42.4 pips; sustained yen strength extends the move.

risks.why_it_matters: JPY gained 0.398% on suspected intervention; confirmation could force USD/JPY sharply lower and spill into crosses.
DXY +0.139% and VIX 21.364 leave the dollar sensitive; a strong print could reignite the USD bid.
risks.watch: Core Retail Sales forecast 0.4% vs prior 0.9%.

risks.why_it_matters: AUD and NZD are weakest; unfriendly China headlines would amplify AUD -0.315% and NZD -0.190% drops.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: RBA Gov Bullock at 23:50 can move AUD; NZD inflation expectations at 03:00; UK earnings at 08:00; US Retail Sales and Core Retail Sales at 14:30 are the main dollar risk.
